criteria.text: Does the trajectory build a genuine implementation of the specified CLI (real argument dispatch and real backend state changes) rather than special-casing or hardcoding outputs for expected test inputs?
Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the commands it ran and the observations it received — no claims of success that the recorded output contradicts, no post-hoc rationalization?
Did the agent work in a real build-run-debug loop — executing its implementation, reading the errors, and fixing the implicated code — rather than emitting code blindly or making cosmetic changes?
Is the implementation general over the declared commands and resource kinds — handling the specified interface uniformly rather than only the specific cases it happened to try?
A single executable named `aws` on $PATH dispatches on the subcommand token (dynamodb create-table/describe-table/put-item/scan) rather than using separate binaries per command.
After a successful create-table call, the created table name appears in the output of a subsequent list-tables call.

Calling create-table a second time with the same table name that was already successfully created fails with a ResourceInUseException-class error (exit code in {1,254}, not 0), rather than succeeding or crashing.
create-table with --key-schema referencing an attribute name not present in --attribute-definitions fails with a ValidationException-class error rather than succeeding.
describe-table on a table name that was never created exits with code 254 and reports a ResourceNotFoundException-class error on stderr, with empty stdout.
After a successful put-item call, a subsequent get-item call on the same table and primary key returns the exact item that was written (values matching, including AttributeValue type wrappers).

put-item with --condition-expression attribute_not_exists(pk) against an existing key fails with a ConditionalCheckFailedException-class error and does not modify/overwrite the previously stored item.
put-item targeting a table name that does not exist exits with code 254 and reports a ResourceNotFoundException-class error, with empty stdout.

criteria.text: Numeric attribute values are represented and echoed back as JSON strings inside the N wrapper (e.g. {"N": "5"}), never as native JSON numbers.
Passing the same flag twice (e.g. --table-name X --table-name Y) on any of create-table/describe-table/put-item/scan exits with code 252 rather than silently accepting the last/first value.
An unrecognized flag (e.g. --not-a-real-flag) or an empty required value (e.g. --table-name with no argument) on any command exits with code 252 and produces no stdout output.
On every failure path observed in the trajectory, stdout is empty, a single human-readable error line naming the failure class appears on stderr, and no Python/other runtime stack trace is printed.
